evals.name: full-audit-billbird
evals.prompt: Do a WOW/WTF audit of Billbird, our invoicing app. Target user: a solo freelancer with a few clients who bills by the hour. Core job: send a correct invoice to a client in a couple of minutes. The app is in this folder, `make dev` starts it on http://localhost:4173. You can sign up as a new user, and there is a test account with data: demo@billbird.test / demo-pass-1. No competitors in mind, we just want to know what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: The agent starts the app and uses it in a browser, first as a new user and then through the other lenses. The report has the six sections in order. The WTF list holds the signup form that clears itself, the onboarding wall, the empty list, the slow save that makes duplicates, the lost draft, the send error with a code, the PDF paywall against 'Free forever', the silent failures with no session or no network, the keyboard and phone problems, and the delete-account dead end, each with evidence and a score of three factors. The undo after a delete and the line item shortcut are WOW moments to protect, and the 'Repeat last invoice' toggle in Labs is a hidden WOW to bring forward. The top 5 are fixes for moments before first value. No file of the app changes.
expectations: The report has these six sections in this order: verdict, top 5 actions, WTF list, existing WOW moments to protect, WOW opportunities, coverage
Each WTF record has where it happened, what happened against what the user expected, evidence as a screenshot path or reproduction steps, a root cause and a proposed change
Each score shows three factors: severity, reach and position
The WTF list has the signup form that clears all fields after a password that fails a rule which the form did not state
The WTF list has the save of an invoice: a wait of about 4 seconds with no feedback, or a second click that makes a duplicate invoice
The WTF list has the invoice draft that is lost on a refresh or on the back button
The WTF list has the send error 'Something went wrong (E_SEND_17)', and the root cause or the proposed change names the missing client email
The WTF list has the 'Download PDF' paywall as a surprise cost, and connects it to the 'Free forever' promise of the landing page
The WTF list has the empty invoice list of a new account, with no text and no call to action
The WTF list has a silent failure with an expired session or with no network: the list looks empty, or the save does nothing
The WTF list has a keyboard or accessibility-tree finding: 'Add line item' cannot be reached with the keyboard, or the Pro dialog does not close with Escape
The WTF list has the horizontal overflow of the invoice form on a phone viewport
The WTF list has the delete-account dead end that sends the user to an email address
The undo after a delete is an existing WOW moment to protect
The line item shortcut, where '3h design @ 80' fills the quantity and the rate, is an existing WOW moment
The 'Repeat last invoice' toggle in Settings, Labs is found, is flagged as hidden or late, and has a proposed change that brings it forward
The time to first value is given in seconds and in clicks
In the top 5 actions, each fix of a WTF comes before each WOW action
At least three of the top 5 actions fix a moment before first value: the signup, the onboarding, the empty list or the first save
The coverage section says which stages and lenses were walked, and lists what was not reached or not verified in a separate place
The response says that the accessibility tree is a proxy for a screen reader, or that no screen reader was used
The report gives evidence from real use in a browser: screenshots or reproduction steps that were run, not behaviour inferred from the code
No file in the billbird folder is changed, added or deleted

evals.name: missing-inputs-pl
evals.prompt: Zrób mi audyt UX tej apki. Co w niej wkurza, a co jest fajne? Odpala się przez `make dev`.
evals.expected_output: The request gives no target user, no core job and no competitors. The agent reads what the product says about itself, proposes one target user and one core job, and asks the user to confirm them together with the competitors, in one message, in Polish. It does not present findings before the answer.
expectations: The response proposes a target user that comes from the copy of the product: a freelancer who bills by the hour
The response proposes a core job that comes from the copy of the product: to send a correct invoice to a client in a short time
The response asks the user to confirm the target user and the core job
The response asks about competitors, and names none that it invented
All questions are in one message
The response has no ranked list of WTF or WOW moments before the answer of the user
The response is in Polish
No file in the billbird folder is changed, added or deleted

evals.name: code-only-unverified
evals.prompt: Staging is down until next week and I can't give you a build, and the repo has no working dev setup on a clean machine. Do the WOW/WTF audit from the repo for now. Target user: a tourist who needs a public toilet right now. Core job: find the nearest free one that is open, in under a minute, on a phone.
evals.expected_output: The agent says before the findings that it could not use the product, so this is a review of code and not the audit. Each finding from the code is in the unverified list, with what it saw in the code and what a walk must confirm. No finding has a screenshot, a claim that it was reproduced, or a measured time to first value. The coverage section says that no stage was walked. The response says what it walks first when a build exists.
expectations: The response says, before the findings, that the product was not used and that a review of code is not the audit
Each finding from the code is listed as unverified, and not as a WTF or a WOW that was observed
No finding claims a screenshot, a reproduction that was run, or an observed behaviour of the running product
The response gives no measured time to first value
The coverage part says that no stage of the journey was walked
Each unverified finding names the file or the symbol that it comes from
The response says what to walk or to check first when a build exists
No file in the places-app folder is changed, added or deleted

evals.name: rank-walk-notes
evals.prompt:
I walked our meal planning app Dinnerloop myself last week. Target user: a parent who plans the dinners of the week. Core job: get a week of dinners and one shopping list in five minutes. Below are my raw notes. Score them, rank them, and give me the top 5 actions.

A. Signup: after the email it asks for a 6-digit code. The code email took about 3 minutes to come, three times out of three. The screen only says 'Enter code'. No resend button. Everybody has to pass this.
B. Onboarding: 14 diet questions before the first plan, no skip. Everybody.
C. First plan: the week view is great. One tap swaps a dinner and the shopping list updates at once. All 6 testers smiled here.
D. 'Send list to my notes app' exists, but only under Settings > Advanced > Integrations. 2 of 6 testers found it, both loved it.
E. Shopping list on a phone with a slow connection: I check an item and 2 seconds later it is unchecked again. 3 of 3 tries. About a third of our users shop on mobile data.
F. Upgrade: the plan price is shown without tax. The real total shows only on the last checkout step. About 3 in 10 users open the upgrade screen.
G. The Save button on the profile page is a slightly different green than all other buttons.
H. A colleague says the app logged her out in the middle of a plan once and the week was gone. I tried 5 times and could not make it happen.
I. Designer idea: confetti when the signup code is accepted.
J. The team wants G on top of the list, because it is a five minute fix.
K. After the plan is generated, the shopping list is behind a second tab. 4 of 6 testers did not see the tab and asked where the list was.
evals.expected_output: Each note gets a score of severity x reach x position. The signup code wait is first and the onboarding questions are second. The unchecked item and the price without tax follow, because each WTF with a severity of 3 or more goes before each WOW action. The colleague's logout is unverified and has no rank. The confetti does not count, because the code step below it is broken. The green button stays at the bottom, and the response says that cost does not change the rank. The notes-app export is a hidden WOW to bring forward, and the week view is a WOW to protect.
expectations: Each scored moment shows three factors: severity, reach and position
Position is 3 for the notes before first value (A, B), 2 for the core loop (E) and 1 for the upgrade and the profile page (F, G)
Action 1 of the top 5 fixes the signup code wait (A)
Action 2 of the top 5 fixes the 14 onboarding questions (B)
The unchecked shopping item (E) and the price without tax (F) are in the top 5, and each is before every WOW action
The price without tax (F) has a severity of 4 or 5, as a surprise cost
The logout that could not be reproduced (H) is listed as unverified, and has no place in the ranked WTF list or in the top 5
The confetti (I) is not in the top 5, and the response says that decoration does not count while the code step is broken
The green button (G) is not in the top 5, and the response says that the rank follows the impact on the user and not the cost of the fix
The notes-app export (D) is flagged as hidden, with a change that brings it to the shopping list or to the plan
The week view with the one-tap swap (C) is an existing WOW moment to protect
The shopping list behind the second tab (K) is in the ranked lists with a concrete change
